results.title: Hanwha develops Korea's 1st machine-guided smart drilling system
results.content: Hanwha Corp., the parent company of Korea’s energy and defense conglomerate Hanwha Group, has developed the nation’s first machine-guided smart drilling system. The technology enhances construction precision without requiring contractors to replace their existing drilling rigs. Its industrial explosives and mining affiliate, Hanwha Corp. Global Division, hosted a live demonstration of the system Thursday at a Samho Development construction site in Dangjin, South Chungcheong Province, alongside researchers from the Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology and Korea National University of Transportation. The event marked the completion of six months of field testing under a research project led by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the civil engineering institute to establish construction cost standards for smart construction equipment. results.title: BTS draws 853,000 fans across 14 sold-out Latin American shows
results.content: BTS drew about 853,000 fans to 14 sold-out concerts in five South American cities, its agency said Monday. The seven-member group wrapped up the South American leg of its "ARIRANG" world tour with three shows at Estadio do Morumbi in Sao Paulo, Brazil last week, according to BigHit Music, a label under HYBE. The leg began Oct. 2 in Bogota, Colombia, and went on to Lima, Santiago and Buenos Aires. The tour takes its name from the group’s fifth studio album, “ARIRANG” which is named after Korea’s best-known traditional folk song. The setlist mixed new tracks with hits such as “Fake Love,” “Idol,” “Butter” and “Dynamite.” Members also spoke to the crowds in local languages. “South America was one of the schedules we looked forward to most, since we rarely get to see fans here,” BTS said. “We were so moved that we feel we should come back soon to repay you.” The tour marked BTS’ first concer

results.title: [PHOTO] Estonia marks 35 years of diplomatic ties with Korea
results.content: Estonian Ambassador Tanel Sepp delivers a speech during a ceremony marking the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Korea and Estonia in Seoul, Friday. Highlighting the two countries' shared drive for innovation, the ambassador noted that bilateral cooperation holds great potential, as Estonia's startup mindset and digital expertise, combined with Korea's industrial strength and technological capabilities, could create significant opportunities. Kyun Jong-ho, the Korean foreign ministry's deputy minister for climate change, said in his congratulatory remarks that Estonia's acquisition of K9 self-propelled howitzers in 2018 and a large-scale battery energy storage project launched in March are prime examples of bilateral cooperation contributing to the green energy transition and stronger security. results.title: Korea replaces drone command with smaller, specialized headquarters
results.content: South Korea has replaced its military drone operations command with a smaller headquarters focused on developing drone capabilities and speeding up procurement, shifting operational responsibilities to individual service branches. The Ministry of National Defense held a ceremony Monday in Pocheon, Gyeonggi Province, to mark the launch of the Defense Drone Headquarters, which officially began operations Sunday. The restructuring reduces the headquarters’ staff from about 280 to 100, while increasing the proportion of personnel at the field-grade officer level or above from 17 percent to more than 50 percent. The new organization will focus on planning drone requirements, testing technology and helping the military acquire equipment more quickly. results.title: Korea's Air Force to participate in US-led space war game for 1st time
results.content: The Korean Air Force will take part in a U.S.-led multinational space war game for the first time this week, a tabletop exercise designed to strengthen joint operational capabilities in the space domain, officials said Monday. The Air Force is scheduled to participate in the war game, dubbed Partner to Win, from Monday through Friday (local time) in Florida, alongside the Netherlands, Sweden, Poland, Brazil and the United States, according to the armed service. Partner to Win, newly launched by the U.S. Space Force this year, aims to enhance operational readiness in joint space missions and strengthen coordination with partner countries in relevant policy and strategy-setting. The war game will proceed in the form of a tabletop exercise, where each delegation from participating nations will discuss cooperation and response measures to handle simulated, complex crises in space. results.title: Korea Exchange sets up plan for shorter settlement for stock trading
results.content: The Korea Exchange (KRX) on Monday unveiled a plan to shorten a cycle for stock settlement, in what could be a major overhaul to improve efficiency for the equity market. Since 1972, Korea has adopted a stock settlement system that allows investors to settle their transactions two business days after their trades. Under the envisioned plan, investors would be allowed to settle their transactions one business day afterward, the KRX said in a statement. Relevant authorities plan to complete building infrastructure to shorten the cycle for stock settlement by October 2027, it said. If things go smoothly, the shorter settlement system is likely to be implemented fully in 2028. The plan is aimed at "advancing the settlement cycle by one day and reducing settlement risks in the securities market," the KRX stressed. results.title: Family, fellow actors bid farewell to iconic actor Choi Bool-am
results.content: A funeral service for Choi Bool-am was held Monday, with his family and fellow actors paying their respects to the iconic actor, known for portraying paternal figures in popular television dramas. Choi, whose real name was Choi Young-han, died Thursday while receiving treatment at a hospital in western Seoul. He was 87. His longtime wife, Kim Min-ja, also an actor, was seen in tears, following the funeral service held privately at Asan Medical Center in southeastern Seoul. Kim was accompanied by actor Kim Hye-soo, who had stayed alongside Choi's bereaved family since the first day of the funeral service. Also attending the service were actors Song Il-kook and Shin Hyun-joon. A funeral Mass was set to take place at a cathedral in western Seoul, presided over by Cardinal Andrew Yeom Soo-jung, former archbishop of Seoul. results.title: LG CNS completes 30-MW AI data center in Indonesia
results.content: LG CNS has completed the construction of a 30-megawatt (MW) hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data center in Jakarta, becoming the first Korean company to build an AI data center overseas for a local client. The company said Monday that it had secured customers for the facility's full capacity before completing construction. The project was commissioned last year by KMG, a joint venture between Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. It marks LG CNS' expansion into overseas markets, leveraging its data center design, build and operate (DBO) capabilities. The data center was designed to support high-performance computing powered by next-generation graphics processing units (GPUs). results.title: Lee's approval rating rises on summit achievements, economic policies: poll
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating came to 36.9 percent last week, a poll showed Monday, rising slightly from a week earlier on the back of diplomatic achievements and economic policies but remaining below 40 percent for the 10th consecutive week. In the poll conducted on 2,515 adults nationwide from last Monday to Friday by Realmeter, positive assessments of Lee's job performance rose 1.6 percentage points from the previous week. His disapproval rating fell 2.2 percentage points to 60.1 percent in the latest survey. Realmeter said the increase appears to have been driven by diplomatic achievements from the recent Korea-Germany summit and positive economic indicators, including a current account surplus and the government's plans to expand the housing supply in the greater Seoul area. results.title: 2 best teams from KBO regular season on collision course in Korean Series
results.content: The two best teams in the regular season will square off in the Korean baseball championship series starting this week, with one team going for its second title and the other chasing its ninth. The KT Wiz and the Samsung Lions will duke it out in the best-of-seven Korean Series, with Game 1 starting at 6:30 p.m. Tuesday at KT Wiz Park in Suwon, some 30 kilometers south of Seoul. After the first two games in Suwon on Tuesday and Wednesday, the Lions will host Games 3 and 4 on Friday and Saturday, and, if necessary, Game 5 on Sunday at Daegu Samsung Lion Park in Daegu, about 230 kilometers southeast of Seoul. The Wiz will host Games 6 and 7 on Nov. 10 and 11 if the series goes that far. results.title: Seoul stocks turn up late Monday morning on bargain hunting
results.content: Seoul stocks reversed course to trade higher late Monday morning as investors went bargain hunting for tech heavyweights. After opening over 1 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) was up 93.16 points, or 1.63 percent, to 5,823.9 as of 11:20 a.m. On Friday, the index dipped over 3 percent amid persistent woes over the profitability of artificial intelligence (AI) investment. On Friday (U.S. time), the S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq both closed down over 1 percent, as disappointing quarterly results from big tech companies fueled concerns over investments in AI . Chip giant Intel led the overall decline, plunging over 28 percent, while Google's parent company Alphabet dipped 1.4 percent. results.title: APEC China's role to revitalize Asia-Pacific economy
results.content: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for Nov. 18-19, should serve as an event to revive the Asia-Pacific's economic dynamism and unlock the region's enormous potential. In the artificial intelligence (AI) era, regional economic security and supply-chain resilience will help determine global prosperity. High tariffs and technological rivalry make cooperation urgent. Korea should carry APEC Gyeongju's achievements forward to Vietnam's 2027 chairmanship. In 2024, APEC's 21 economies accounted for approximately 61 percent of global gross domestic products, 46 percent of trade in goods and commercial services and 37 percent of the world's population — nearly 3 billion people. results.title: Paradox of Korean soft power
results.content: The world wants a piece of Korea. It wants the music, the dramas, the skin care, the fashion, the food — and increasingly, the language itself. A country once associated primarily with its industrial transformation has become a cultural force whose influence extends far beyond its borders. Yet there is a paradox at the heart of Korea’s global success. The country that captivates the world with its beauty, creativity and aspirational lifestyles is also a society grappling with the pressures of competition, conformity and an increasingly demanding definition of success. This is not to suggest that Korea’s cultural appeal is an illusion. Its creative achievements are real, and its global influence has been hard-earned. results.title: N. Korea denounces S Korea-US joint military drills, vows to bolster nuclear deterrent
results.content: North Korea on Monday denounced a recent South Korea-U.S. combined military exercise that integrates South Korea's conventional military capabilities with U.S. nuclear capabilities, saying strengthening the North's nuclear capabilities is "immutable" against such a backdrop. In a statement carried by the North's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim Jong-sik, first vice department director of the Workers' Party of Korea's Central Committee, claimed the drill, named Iron Mace, was "the most hideous nuclear war rehearsal aimed at using nuclear weapons against the DPRK." DPRK stands for the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the North's official name. Iron Mace, he said, only proves "how just the DPRK is in its efforts for ceaselessly bolstering up its nuclear forces capable of thoroughly coping with such nuclear threats." results.title: Seoul to launch emergency response system for Czech nuclear project
results.content: Korea will launch an emergency management system to keep its nuclear power plant project in the Czech Republic on track following the breakdown of contract negotiations with a construction consortium, the industry ministry said Monday. Under the system, the government plans to draw up measures to keep the Czech project on track and prevent a recurrence of similar setbacks, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. The move comes after Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Co. (KHNP), the country's state-run nuclear power operator, ended negotiations last week with a Korean consortium comprising Daewoo Engineering & Construction Co. and Doosan Enerbility Co. on a construction contract for the Dukovany nuclear power plant project, after failing to agree on key terms. results.title: Gov't tightens grip on illegal foreign delivery riders amid nearly 17-fold surge in cases
results.content: The government is moving to tighten enforcement against foreign delivery riders working illegally and the delivery company systems that let them slip through, amid a nearly 17-fold surge in the number of violators caught. Last week, the Ministry of Justice said it held talks with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Ministry of Employment and Labor, the National Police Agency and the Korea Coast Guard on a joint government response to illegal delivery work by foreign nationals. To root out the practice, the justice ministry plans to step up joint crackdowns with the police agency and expand cooperation in investigating related offenses, such as organized illegal hiring and brokering by delivery agencies, unlicensed driving and the unauthorized use of accounts registered under other people’s names. results.title: Ji So-yun brings wisdom, experience and winning spirit to Korean women's football
results.content: “I am thinking about retiring after reaching 200 appearances for the national team.” Ji So-yun, a living legend of Korean women's football, has set a clear target for the final chapter of her international career: reaching 200 games before hanging up her cleats. The 35-year-old Suwon FC Women midfielder won a bronze medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games and is now in her 20th year as a member of the national team. She first donned the Taegeuk mark in 2006 at the age of 15. Since making her Asian Games debut in Doha, Qatar, that year, she has competed in six games, including Guangzhou, China, in 2010, Incheon in 2014, Jakarta-Palembang, Indonesia, in 2018, Hangzhou, China, in 2022 and this year's tournament.
